transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-04
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Ethan Brooks (Redwood); Liam O'Connor, Renee Park, Marco Díaz, Hannah Li (ZeroSum)

Summary (auto):
Discussed pilot scope for ZeroSum Insurance - focus on authentication (SSO/SAML), RBAC and audit logging, data residency and private VPC option. Agreed on success criteria (p99 latency target, throughput targets, model fidelity checks), initial benchmark plan, and deliverables for SOC2/ISO documentation.

Topics:
- Security requirements (SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC)
- Pilot environment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC)
- Benchmarking plan and success criteria (latency, throughput, token sizes)
- Timeline and procurement gating

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to run through the pilot scope and make sure we capture the security gating early so you don't hit any surprises, um Liam you wanna kick off with where ZeroSum is at?
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: yeah thanks Maya, um quick context, we support claims processing and some underwriting tooling, PII in the workflows is redacted but the business wants the model running inside our control plane. We're evaluating both hosted with strict controls and private VPC. Main asks: SOC2, ISO, SSO for user access, RBAC for role separation, and immutable audit logs. Timeline: procurement wants an internal pilot by end of June, ideally production in Q4.
[00:42] Maya Patel: got it, that's helpful. Renee, from security side is there anything else?
[00:48] Renee Park: yeah hi, um two quick things. One, we need the SOC 2 Type II report and ISO attestation, and two, encryption at rest with customer-managed keys ideally - KMS/HSM integration. Also we need logs forwarded to our SIEM, we use Splunk. Audit log fidelity: must include request/response metadata, user id, model version, and a cryptographic timestamp if possible.
[01:15] Ethan Brooks: just to clarify, when you say request/response do you need full response bodies in the audit trail or metadata only? Full bodies would be bigger and may raise storage/residency concerns.
[01:29] Renee Park: metadata is primary, but for certain escalations we will need full redacted outputs. So ability to export traces on demand is a must.
[01:36] Marco Dedaz: adding to that, for the ML team we'll need token-level latency and per-request KV cache hit rate to understand effective speedups. Also can you support per-model version tagging so we can trace regressions?
[01:52] Ethan Brooks: yes per-model version tagging is supported, we can produce per-token timing and cache stats in the console, and export as CSV. For KV cache hit rate, we can expose those metrics and the latency percentiles.
[02:05] Hannah Li: procurement question: what does pilot pricing look like and are there minimums for dedicated capacity?
[02:12] Maya Patel: we'll share a pilot pricing sheet after this call. For dedicated capacity we typically have a short-term reserved pool for pilots, no long term commitment for a 6-week pilot, but production commitments will change the pricing.
[02:24] Liam O'Connor: timeline wise, can you provision a private VPC environment quickly?
[02:29] Ethan Brooks: yes, we can provision a private VPC with customer-managed keys; typical lead time is 3-7 business days once we have the network peering info and an infra contact. Our onboarding playbook is in the shared folder - I'll link it.
[02:43] Maya Patel: I'll also add the SOC2/ISO artifacts and the short architecture diagram to the shared drive after the meeting.
[02:49] Renee Park: on SSO, we use SAML 2.0 with attribute-based groups - we need SCIM provisioning and SAML sign-on for Redwood console access, along with RBAC mapping to our roles.
[03:04] Ethan Brooks: we support SAML and SCIM; RBAC mapping is configurable and we can map your groups to role sets (admin, reviewer, observer, engineer). There's also an API for provisioning service accounts.
[03:16] Liam O'Connor: okay good. For data residency, certain PII flows must not leave eu-west-1; are regional deployments available?
[03:25] Maya Patel: yes we have region pinning for data and private deployments in specific cloud regions. For strict residency we recommend private VPC or on-prem package.
[03:34] Marco Dedaz: benchmarks - our rough production SLOs: p95 under 120ms, p99 under 300ms for 512 token sequences, baseline cost target X (we'll share target numbers), and sustained concurrency of 60 requests per second with bursts to 400. We want to run a 2-hour soak and a 1-hour stress test.
[03:58] Ethan Brooks: that's helpful. For the pilot we usually run three phases: baseline single-worker latency, concurrency ramp to your sustained rate, and then burst stress. For your sequence lengths and token averages do you have sample traces you can share?
[04:12] Marco Dedaz: yes I'll anonymize and share traces, average token length ~140, 95th at 520. Also some requests include short function calls and structured outputs.
[04:23] Ethan Brooks: noted. For hardware we recommend A100 or H100 for the stress runs, but we can run quantized variants on Ampere lower footprint for cost-based comparisons. There may be small fidelity diffs with 4-bit quantization, we can measure that.
[04:40] Renee Park: how do you handle keys for private deployments? KMS integration or HSM required?
[04:46] Ethan Brooks: we support customer-managed KMS in cloud (AWS KMS) and HSM integrations for on-prem. Keys never leave the customer's key control plane for private.
[04:56] Liam O'Connor: audit logging - can logs be forwarded to our Splunk with TLS and signed delivery; retention policy is 7 years for certain records, is that a problem?
[05:06] Maya Patel: we can stream logs via secure forwarders to Splunk; long-term retention is usually handled by the customer SIEM - we can push to an S3 bucket in your account if needed.
[05:16] Hannah Li: procurement needs an acceptance criteria doc we can review. What do you usually put in acceptance?
[05:23] Maya Patel: typical acceptance criteria for pilots: 1) functional parity vs baseline model (we do evals vs your labeled prompts), 2) p99 latency under agreed threshold for typical sequences, 3) throughput targets met for N-hour soak, 4) security checks: SOC2/ISO docs reviewed, SSO/SCIM working, RBAC enforced, audit logs validated. We'll share a templated acceptance doc.
[05:49] Marco Dedaz: on fidelity tests, can Redwood run automated evals against a prompt set and provide diff reports?
[05:56] Ethan Brooks: yes we have an eval harness; we can run A/B diffs and output similarity metrics like ROUGE/BLEU where applicable and custom thresholds you define.
[06:07] Renee Park: about model fallbacks and graceful degradation - if the dedicated pool is saturated can you route to a cheaper hosted model while preserving residency and compliance? That's a hard ask.
[06:18] Ethan Brooks: fallback to hosted with residency is tricky; for strict residency you'd need private VPC variants in each region. We can do model variant fallbacks within the private fleet (lower precision/throughput optimized), but not cross-region hosted without compliance sign-off.
[06:33] Liam O'Connor: ok that's acceptable. For the benchmark instrumentation what metrics will you provide?
[06:39] Ethan Brooks: token throughput, request QPS, per-token latency breakdown, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, memory, and model version. We'll provide dashboards and raw CSV exports.
[06:50] Maya Patel: let's get more concrete on the benchmark plan - initial baseline run we ask for 50 concurrent clients, sequence=256, avg tokens=140, for 30 minutes. Then ramp to 60 RPS sustained for 2 hours, and then burst to 400 RPS for 10 minutes. Does that align with your expectations?
[07:12] Marco Dedaz: yes that's pretty close - can you also capture a 95th/99th percentile on CPU and GPU stalls? We had issues with KV cache pressure last time.
[07:21] Ethan Brooks: will do. We'll include cache eviction metrics and per-request memory.
[07:28] Hannah Li: procurement - are there standard security addendums or can we use our master services agreement?
[07:34] Maya Patel: we usually start with our standard MSA and can consider customer's redlines; for pilots we try not to negotiate major legal terms. We'll surface the security addendum that covers SOC2/ISO attestations and data handling.
[07:46] Renee Park: one more on RBAC - we need ability to enforce session timeouts, MFA enforcement, and anomaly detection alerts hooked into our PagerDuty.
[07:56] Ethan Brooks: session controls and MFA are supported; integration with PagerDuty for alerting is supported via webhook. Anomaly detection requires forwarding logs to your SIEM; we can add sample rules for detection.
[08:09] Liam O'Connor: is there a way to redact or mask PII in responses before storing logs?
[08:14] Ethan Brooks: yes we offer hooks for post-processing - either client-side redaction or Redwood-side redaction via configurable filters. For the pilot we'll recommend client-side so you own the redaction keys.
[08:26] Marco Dedaz: about model version pinning - can we pin a specific hash and roll forward with canary? We need to trace regressions to specific code changes.
[08:35] Ethan Brooks: absolutely. Our rollout supports canary percentages, A/B, and automatic rollback on regression alerts. Each request includes model hash metadata.
[08:44] Maya Patel: quick note - I'll upload a short checklist for the pilot gating: security docs, infra contacts, sample traffic, acceptance criteria, pricing, and timeline.
[08:53] Marco Dedaz: on the fidelity delta, what are acceptable thresholds, do you support embedding-based similarity checks?
[09:00] Ethan Brooks: yes we can run embedding similarity or n-gram diffs, and produce aggregated deltas. We also support human review queue integrations.
[09:08] Liam O'Connor: procurement - can you send an estimated cost for two scenarios: hosted with strict controls vs dedicated private VPC with CMK?
[09:17] Maya Patel: yes we'll send two estimates in the pricing doc - include expected token volumes and concurrency assumptions.
[09:23] Hannah Li: are there any third-party security certifications we should be aware of?
[09:29] Maya Patel: we maintain SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; we also have a penetration test report summary available. We'll share those as part of the package.
[09:39] Renee Park: about data lifecycle - we need guarantees around deletion requests, how quickly can you purge logs and cached KV data for escrows?
[09:49] Ethan Brooks: for private VPC we can perform data purge within 24-72 hours depending on the storage tier; we'll provide an API for purge requests and a certificate of deletion. For hosted, we have retention policies and can do expedited purge with a support ticket.
[10:03] Marco Dedaz: ok good. For the bench runs do you need us to provide a synthetic workload tool or do you want Redwood to drive it?
[10:12] Ethan Brooks: we can provide a bench harness (JMeter-based) and also accept your traces to replay; recommended to do both. We'll host the harness in the shared folder.
[10:22] Liam O'Connor: let's talk acceptance criteria again - for fidelity we'll set a threshold of 95% similarity across our golden prompt set and p99 latency under 300ms for sequences <=512. If both are met plus security checks cleared we sign off.
[10:39] Maya Patel: that's clear and actionable. We'll reflect that in the acceptance doc.
[10:44] Renee Park: last question - will you provide a list of sub-processors for hosted infrast- infra? We need to run through our vendor assessment.
[10:53] Maya Patel: yes we'll provide a sub-processor list and the SOC2 coverage map.
[10:58] Marco Dedaz: any concerns on Redwood side about running the evals with our samples? Data sensitivity?
[11:05] Ethan Brooks: we prefer anonymized samples but if there's sensitive content we can run the bench in your VPC so data never leaves.
[11:12] Liam O'Connor: ok, next steps?
[11:15] Maya Patel: action items recap: I'll send docs (SOC2, ISO, MSA seed) and the acceptance template; Ethan will stand up the bench plan and run baseline and share results; Marco will upload traces; Liam/Hannah will confirm procurement timeline. We'll aim to start bench the week of June 8.
[11:33] Hannah Li: sounds good, procurement will try to confirm timeline by next Tuesday.
[11:37] Maya Patel: perfect. Anything else from anyone?
[11:40] Renee Park: please include our security contact in the share, that's renee.park@zerosum-ins.com.
[11:46] Maya Patel: will do. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the first bench slot.
[11:53] Liam O'Connor: thanks all.

End of transcript.
